test_cases.title: Create CAPA from Approved Deviation
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in with QA Specialist role. A deviation exists with status 'Closed' or 'Approved', containing a deviation number, product name, and root cause category.
steps: Navigate to the approved deviation record.
Click the 'Create CAPA' button.
Review the prepopulated CAPA form fields.
Save the CAPA record.
test_cases.expected: The new CAPA record is successfully created, and the fields for deviation number, product, and root cause category exactly match the source deviation.

test_cases.title: Prevent CAPA Creation from Deviation Under Investigation
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in with QA Specialist role. A deviation exists with status 'Under Investigation'.
steps: Navigate to the deviation record that is 'Under Investigation'.
Attempt to click or locate the 'Create CAPA' button.
test_cases.expected: The 'Create CAPA' button is either disabled or hidden, and attempting to force creation via API returns an error stating that a CAPA cannot be created from a deviation under investigation.

test_cases.title: Audit Trail Recording for CAPA Creation
test_cases.preconditions: User 'QA_User01' is logged in. An eligible approved deviation exists.
steps: Create a CAPA from the approved deviation.
Navigate to the system audit trail for the newly created CAPA.
test_cases.expected: An audit trail entry exists recording the CAPA creation event, displaying the exact user ID ('QA_User01'), and the correct system date and timestamp.

test_cases.title: Unauthorized User Attempts CAPA Creation
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in with a 'Warehouse Operator' role (non-QA role). An eligible approved deviation exists.
steps: Navigate to the approved deviation record.
Check for the presence of the 'Create CAPA' action or button.
test_cases.expected: The 'Create CAPA' action is not visible or accessible to the Warehouse Operator, enforcing 21 CFR Part 11 security boundaries.

test_cases.title: Successfully assign CAPA action with valid details
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in as a CAPA owner and a draft CAPA record exists.
steps: Navigate to the CAPA action assignment section.
Enter a valid action description.
Select exactly one valid user as the assignee.
Enter a future due date within the allowed timeframe and click Save.
test_cases.expected: The action is successfully created with one assignee, description, and due date. An automated notification email is sent to the assignee.

test_cases.title: Attempt to assign CAPA action without an assignee
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in as a CAPA owner.
steps: Navigate to the CAPA action assignment section.
Enter a valid action description and due date.
Leave the assignee field blank and click Save.
test_cases.expected: The system prevents saving and displays a validation error stating that an assignee is required.

test_cases.title: Attempt to assign CAPA action with a past due date
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in as a CAPA owner.
steps: Navigate to the CAPA action assignment section.
Enter a valid action description and assignee.
Select a due date set to yesterday's date and click Save.
test_cases.expected: The system rejects the date and displays a validation error stating due dates must be reasonable (not in the past).

test_cases.title: Unauthorized user attempts to assign a CAPA action
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in with a Read-Only or unauthorized role.
steps: Navigate to a CAPA record action section.
Attempt to input an assignee, description, and due date.
test_cases.expected: The action creation/assignment controls are either disabled or hidden, and saving is blocked with an access-denied error.

test_cases.title: Audit trail and e-signature verification for CAPA action assignment
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in as a CAPA owner and action details are filled out.
steps: Complete all required action fields (assignee, description, due date).
Click Save, provide electronic signature credentials (username/password and meaning), and confirm.
Navigate to the system Audit Trail for the CAPA record.
test_cases.expected: An immutable audit trail record is generated capturing the old value, new value, timestamp, user ID, and the e-signature reason for the action creation.

ambiguities: Acceptance criterion 2 states 'Due dates must be reasonable', but does not define the exact business rules or thresholds for what constitutes a 'reasonable' due date (e.g., maximum allowable days in the future or relation to the CAPA target closure date).

test_cases.title: Successful Escalation of Overdue CAPA Action
test_cases.preconditions: A CAPA action is assigned to a user and its due date has passed by the configured threshold.
steps: Trigger the automated escalation job or wait for the scheduled execution interval.
Log into the system as the designated manager.
Navigate to the CAPA Action Escalation dashboard.
test_cases.expected: The system automatically flags the action as 'Escalated', sends an email notification to the manager within the configured quick turnaround window, and displays the overdue action in the manager's escalation queue.

test_cases.title: Non-Escalation of CAPA Action Prior to Due Date
test_cases.preconditions: A CAPA action is active with a due date set for tomorrow.
steps: Run the escalation job manually or allow the background scheduler to run.
Check the status of the CAPA action.
Verify the manager's escalation queue.
test_cases.expected: The CAPA action status remains 'Open' or 'In Progress', and no escalation notification is sent to the manager.

test_cases.title: Escalation Boundary at Exact Due Date Expiry
test_cases.preconditions: A CAPA action due date and time is set to exactly 00:00 UTC today, and the system clock is at 00:01 UTC today.
steps: Execute the escalation background job at 00:01 UTC.
Review the CAPA action status and system logs.
test_cases.expected: The system identifies the action as overdue by 1 minute and successfully triggers the escalation workflow to the manager.

test_cases.title: Unauthorized Role Attempting to Access Escalation Settings
test_cases.preconditions: Logged into the GxP system as a standard 'Operator' role without QA Manager privileges.
steps: Attempt to access the CAPA escalation configuration and management module.
Attempt to manually override or dismiss an escalation.
test_cases.expected: The system denies access with an 'Access Denied' error message and logs a security violation event in the audit trail.

test_cases.title: Audit Trail and Electronic Signature Capture on Escalation Override
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as QA Manager; an action has been escalated.
steps: Navigate to the escalated action.
Perform a manual acknowledgment or extension of the escalated action requiring an e-signature.
Provide user credentials and select a meaniningful e-signature reason, then view the system audit trail.
test_cases.expected: The 21 CFR Part 11 compliant audit trail captures the exact timestamp, user ID, old value, new value (Acknowledged/Extended), and the mandatory e-signature meaning.

ambiguities: Acceptance criteria 2 states 'Escalations happen quickly', but does not define an exact numerical time window (e.g., within 5 minutes, within 1 hour).
Acceptance criteria 1 does not specify the exact hierarchy or rule for identifying 'the manager' (e.g., direct supervisor, department head, or CAPA owner's manager).

test_cases.title: Successful CAPA Closure by QA Manager
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in as QA Manager. CAPA is in 'Pending Closure' state. All associated actions are in 'Closed' status. An effectiveness check plan is attached. Closure summary is exactly 55 characters long.
steps: Navigate to CAPA-204 details page.
Click the 'Close CAPA' button.
Enter valid QA Manager credentials for 21 CFR Part 11 e-signature.
Confirm the closure.
test_cases.expected: The CAPA status updates to 'Closed'. System records an immutable audit trail entry capturing the user ID, timestamp, reason for change, and e-signature manifest.

test_cases.title: Attempt to Close CAPA with Open Actions
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in as QA Manager. CAPA-204 has at least one action in 'In Progress' status.
steps: Navigate to CAPA-204 details page.
Click the 'Close CAPA' button.
test_cases.expected: The system prevents closure and displays an error message: 'CAPA cannot be closed while associated actions remain open.'

test_cases.title: Closure Summary Character Count Boundary Check (Under 50 Characters)
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in as QA Manager. All CAPA actions are closed. Effectiveness check plan is attached.
steps: Navigate to CAPA-204 details page.
Click 'Close CAPA'.
Enter a closure summary containing exactly 49 characters.
Attempt to submit.
test_cases.expected: The system rejects the submission and displays a validation error stating the closure summary must be at least 50 characters.

test_cases.title: CAPA Closure Attempt by Non-QA Manager Role
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in with the 'CAPA Owner' or 'Regular User' role. CAPA-204 has all actions closed and required artifacts attached.
steps: Navigate to CAPA-204 details page.
Attempt to locate and click the 'Close CAPA' button.
test_cases.expected: The 'Close CAPA' button is either hidden or disabled. If forced via API, the system returns a 403 Forbidden error.

test_cases.title: Verification of Audit Trail and 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance on Closure
test_cases.preconditions: CAPA-204 has just been successfully closed by a QA Manager.
steps: Navigate to the system Audit Trail log.
Filter for CAPA-204 events.
test_cases.expected: An audit log entry exists showing the old state, new state ('Closed'), exact timestamp (UTC), user full name, cryptographic signature record, and the reason/meaning of the e-signature.

ambiguities: Acceptance criterion 1 mentions 'evidence is attached' in the user story summary, but acceptance criteria 1 and 2 do not explicitly specify what type of evidence or file formats are mandatory for closure, beyond the effectiveness check plan and closure summary.

test_cases.title: Edit closed CAPA as CAPA Owner (Happy Path)
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in as a CAPA Owner. A CAPA record is in 'Closed' status.
steps: Navigate to the Closed CAPA record.
Click the 'Edit' button.
Modify the 'CAPA Description' field with corrected text.
Click 'Save' and provide a mandatory e-signature reason for change.
test_cases.expected: The system successfully saves the changes, updates the CAPA record, and displays the updated text in the 'CAPA Description' field.

test_cases.title: Edit closed CAPA as unauthorized user (Permission)
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in as a standard Read-Only Viewer (not the CAPA Owner). A CAPA record is in 'Closed' status.
steps: Navigate to the Closed CAPA record.
Observe the available action buttons.
test_cases.expected: The 'Edit' button is either hidden or disabled for the user who is not the CAPA owner.

test_cases.title: Verify Audit Trail and Electronic Signature generation on edit
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in as the CAPA Owner. A CAPA record is in 'Closed' status.
steps: Edit a field on the Closed CAPA record.
Submit the change with e-signature credentials (username, password, meaning).
Navigate to the CAPA Audit Trail.
test_cases.expected: The audit trail records the old value, new value, timestamp, user ID, and the mandatory e-signature reason for change in compliance with 21 CFR Part 11.

test_cases.title: Attempt to edit closed CAPA without providing e-signature reason
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in as the CAPA Owner. A CAPA record is in 'Closed' status.
steps: Edit a field on the Closed CAPA record.
Click 'Save' without entering a reason for change in the e-signature prompt.
test_cases.expected: The system blocks the save action and displays a validation error requiring a mandatory reason for change.

ambiguities: Acceptance criterion 1 states 'The owner can edit any field', but does not specify if system-generated fields (such as Record ID, Creation Date, or Closed Date) are exempt from editing.

test_cases.title: Successful CAPA Effectiveness Check and Approval
test_cases.preconditions: CAPA is in 'Implemented' state and the predefined effectiveness review date has been reached. User is logged in as QA Approver.
steps: Navigate to CAPA-206 details page.
Enter effectiveness check results confirming the action resolved the issue.
Click 'Submit for Approval' and sign with 21 CFR Part 11 compliant electronic signature (username, password, meaning).
test_cases.expected: The system records the effectiveness results as 'Effective', captures the electronic signature details (timestamp, user, meaning), and updates the CAPA status to 'Effectiveness Verified - Closed'.

test_cases.title: Unauthorized User Attempts to Approve Effectiveness
test_cases.preconditions: CAPA effectiveness check results have been entered. User is logged in as a standard Operator without QA Approver privileges.
steps: Navigate to CAPA-206 details page.
Attempt to locate and click the 'Approve Effectiveness' button.
test_cases.expected: The system denies access to the approval function, either by hiding the button or displaying an error message stating 'Insufficient permissions to perform 21 CFR Part 11 approval.'

test_cases.title: Attempting Effectiveness Check Before Scheduled Review Period
test_cases.preconditions: CAPA implementation is complete, but the scheduled effectiveness check date is set 30 days in the future. User is logged in as QA.
steps: Navigate to CAPA-206.
Attempt to initiate and complete the effectiveness check prior to the scheduled date.
test_cases.expected: The system blocks the submission and displays a validation error: 'Effectiveness check cannot be performed before the scheduled review date.'

test_cases.title: Audit Trail Verification for Effectiveness Result Modification
test_cases.preconditions: Effectiveness check results have been initially saved by a QA user.
steps: Log in as a second QA user, modify the effectiveness comments, and save the record.
Navigate to the CAPA-206 Audit Trail.
test_cases.expected: The audit trail captures an immutable log containing the exact timestamp, the user ID of the modifier, the old value, the new value, and the mandatory reason for change.

ambiguities: Acceptance criterion 3 is marked as 'TBD: what happens if the CAPA was not effective', preventing the creation of exact test cases for the failure workflow (e.g., whether it triggers a child CAPA, reopens the existing CAPA, or routes to a specific failure review board).
